newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: TYRE BLOW OUT ONE THEORY INTO BUS CRASH CAUSE
Investigators into yesterday's fatal bus crash in northern New South Wales, have started a physical examination of the bus in a bid to determine the cause of the accident.
Police have confirmed they're investigating the possibility that a tyre blowout caused the accident, which claimed the lives of two people and left about 40 injured.

The McCafferty's coach crashed on the New England Highway, north of Tenterfield, killing the 62 year-old relief driver, Adrian Nickols, of Toowoomba, and 12 year-old Chris Haywood, of Bendemeer, near Tamworth.

Since the accident, there've been renewed calls for seat belts to be fitted on all coaches, after it was revealed that the two people killed were not wearing their seat belts at the time of the accident.
WARNING FOR CYCLONE RACHEL REMAINS CURRENT
A warning for a category two cyclone remains for the inland Pilbara between Millstream and Marble Bar and south to Paraburdoo and Newman including Wittenoom and Munjina.
Rachel is about 165-kilometres south of Port Hedland and travelling south at 15-kilometres an hour.
Destructive winds with gusts to 140-kilometres an hour are expected within 150-kilometres of the cyclone's centre, however the winds are expected to ease in the next 12 hours.
BETTER WEATHER IMPROVES VISIBILITY FOR SEARCH
Better weather in the Southern Ocean has improved visibility, as the search continues for lone British sailor Tony Bullimore.

The Maritime Rescue Co-ordination Centre says the first of four Orions is due to arrive in the search area, about 14-hundred nautical miles south-west of Perth, at about ten-thirty this morning, Eastern Standard Time.
The Authority says Frenchman Thierry Dubois is still drifting in a life raft, waiting to be picked up tomorrow by the frigate -- HMAS Adelaide.
Improved weather conditions have helped the frigate increase speed, but the ship's captain says conditions are expected to worsen by the time it reaches the area tomorrow.
RESCUED SAILOR ON SOLID GROUND
French sailor Raphael Dinelli is in Hobart after a dramatic rescue in the Southern Ocean two weeks ago.
Dinelli was rescued on Boxing Day after the yacht he was sailing in a around-the-world race capsized.
He was rescued by fellow lone sailor, Peter Goss, sailing Aqua Quorum.
Goss decided to take Dinelli into Hobart rather than transfer the Frenchman at sea.
Goss, who will spend two days in Hobart where he will carry out minor repairs, says he's been given an assurance by race organisers that he can continue the race.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
